clue.text: Don't declare to the staff

definitions.meaning: a cricket captain who does not declare an innings closed tells the batsmen to keep batting
a short stick, such as one a conductor or relay runner holds

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a side may declare, ending its innings early; refusing to do so means carrying on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting on is what a side does instead of declaring, and a conductor's or runner's stick is a baton.

clue.text: One insect let free another

parts.note: a bee is one kind of insect

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the word are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: One captured bug lets another one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' is the anagram signal on 'let'; 'another' defines by pointing back to 'One insect', so the answer is a second kind of insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition leans on 'One insect': a beetle is a further kind of insect.

clue.text: Not well tuned to the rising ball

definitions.meaning: singing or playing slightly sharp or flat
in cricket a ball that bounces up from the playing strip comes up from there

explanation.walkthrough: The PITCH in cricket is the strip of turf between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Music out of tune is off key, and a cricket delivery climbs from the strip of turf it bounces on.

clue.text: Vermin invested rot makes for complaint

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the vermin wraps round the rot

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance animal, vermin

explanation.surface: Rats among decaying goods give cause for a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An objection raised against something is a formal complaint.

clue.text: What Henry Tudor wanted for five shillings

definitions.meaning: Henry Tudor fought at Bosworth to win the throne of England
an old British coin worth five shillings, a quarter of a pound

explanation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation Britain had a coin worth five shillings called a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII sought the English throne, symbolised by its royal headgear, and a five-shilling coin was also so named.

clue.text: Kept upsetting American coloured

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the abbreviation upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: stained means coloured, as with a dye

explanation.surface: A Yank kept being disturbed by tinted things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns US into SU at the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained effort is effort kept up over time.

clue.text: Hump-back river-crossing in Cornwall

parts.note: a camel is the animal with a hump on its back
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: A hump-backed bridge over a stream somewhere in the far south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Camelford is a town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip; it stands on the River Camel. 'Hump-back' suggests a bridge but gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a location: Camelford is a small town in that county.

clue.text: Pay for others to yell

definitions.meaning: in British and Australian slang to buy a round of drinks for companions
to cry out loudly

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs, 'my shout' means it is my turn to buy the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing a round is colloquially to treat, and a loud cry is a holler.

clue.text: Pleasant place on the Riviera

definitions.meaning: agreeable, enjoyable
a city on the French Mediterranean coast

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means agreeable, and the city of that name lies on the Côte d'Azur.

clue.text: Tender feeling though it is not a hard pimple

definitions.meaning: an affection or fondness for someone

definitions.text: though it is not a hard pimple
definitions.meaning: read literally, a blemish that is yielding rather than firm

explanation.definitionFit: A fondness is a weakness of affection, and literally a squashy blemish on the skin.

clue.text: Stir up people in sight, in hearing

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read, so the words are said aloud

explanation.surface: A crowd gets roused by people who can be seen and heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' marks that 'in sight' spoken aloud gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke a crowd to action is to rouse them.

clue.text: Weather problem which eliminates poor athletes

definitions.meaning: excessive warmth as a trouble of climate
a qualifying race in which slower runners are knocked out

explanation.definitionFit: A hot spell is a weather trouble, and a preliminary race round knocks out the weaker competitors.

clue.text: Only way to board escalator is to go faster

definitions.meaning: you get onto a moving staircase by placing your foot on it
an informal order to hurry up

explanation.definitionFit: Literally placing your foot on the moving stair, and idiomatically to hurry.

clue.text: Write off suggestion for rescuing man overboard

definitions.meaning: to send a brief letter
literally lowering a rope to someone in the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is a link word; the idiom means send someone a short letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, sending a short note; literally, lowering a rope to someone in the sea.

clue.text: Little doctor ought to give a dose of medicine

parts.note: DR is the short form of doctor
an old spelling variant of aught, meaning anything

explanation.surface: A junior physician should be prescribing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ought' is used in its rare noun sense, an alternative spelling of AUGHT (anything, or zero).
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single measured drink of liquid medicine.

clue.text: See Corfu resort abandon peaceful measures

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Tourists are urged to view the Greek holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place beside Corfu, but read as re-sort it rearranges SEECORFU.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning to violence or compulsion means giving up peaceable means.

clue.text: The one who twists the yarn or turns the ball?

definitions.text: The one who twists the yarn
definitions.meaning: a person or machine that draws fibre into thread
a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off the ground

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler who makes the ball turn sharply off the ground is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread maker twists fibres, and a cricket bowler imparts rotation; both are named for that action.

clue.text: Ignore Jewish feast

definitions.meaning: to leave out or overlook
the spring festival remembering the Exodus from Egypt

explanation.definitionFit: To overlook is to skip someone, and the Exodus festival takes its name from the angel sparing Israelite homes.

clue.text: French ruffians cause pain in uppish health resort

indicators.note: the pain sits inside the resort
in a down clue going up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a spa is a resort with healing waters

explanation.surface: Thugs bring suffering to a stuck-up watering place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppish' turns the resort upward (APS), and 'in' places the pain inside. Apaches were Parisian street gangsters around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used in Paris for violent street thugs of the early 1900s.

clue.text: Drug traffic investigator

parts.note: seems to describe a narcotics detective, but means a police officer who checks motorists going too fast, the drug being slang for amphetamine

explanation.definitionFit: A traffic policeman who catches motorists exceeding the limit; amphetamine is slang 'speed'.

clue.text: Set of rules the enemy would like break to break

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Set of rules the enemy would like break to break': garbled OCR ('break to break' for 'to break'), beyond a letter-level misread and no scan to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: Set of rules the enemy would like break to break

clue.text: Blow to keep the foot warm

definitions.meaning: a punch or hard hit
a knitted garment worn on the foot

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a punch, and the knitted garment pulled over the foot.

clue.text: ADC set to form training corps

indicators.note: the letters are put together to make a new shape

explanation.surface: An aide-de-camp is assigned to set up a military training unit.
explanation.walkthrough: ADC (aide-de-camp, an officer's assistant) is only fodder; 'to form' rearranges ADCSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadet forces are corps of young people undergoing military training.

clue.text: Draws up in the forest glade

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from the bottom

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAWS into its backward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, as found in a woodland clearing.

clue.text: Nut from palm on desert

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A nut grows on a palm tree out in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is an edible nut, the kernel of a stone fruit.

clue.text: Meat cheaper, so do a feller's work

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat
prices that are down are lower

explanation.surface: With the butcher's prices falling, a lumberjack sets about felling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' reads as 'fellow' but is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fells trees brings them to the ground with an axe.

clue.text: Single cut causes a stroke

parts.note: a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: One small wound brings on a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: A snick in cricket is a slight deflection of the ball off the edge of the bat; 'stroke' suggests a medical seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a faint edged shot is called by this name.

clue.text: Right peer salvaged Conservative stock

indicators.note: the word is rescued and rebuilt, so its letters are reassembled

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A right-wing lord rescued Tory shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salvaged' rearranges the peer into EPER; 'stock' here means a theatre's standing stock of plays, not shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's repertory is its stock of plays performed in rotation, hence 'rep' companies.
